verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'water landing around 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R2: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10, off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splash down at around 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10 ... off the coast of Southern California ... 5:07 pm PDT'; R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) ... off the coast of San Diego'; R6: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm exact date, time, timezone conversion, location in Pacific off California/San Diego.

verifications.claim: The crew module began its atmospheric entry at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m.: Entry interface'; R2: 'communications blackout at 7:53 p.m.' during descent through atmosphere; R3: '7:53 p.m. EDT: Entry Interface occurs and the Orion capsule re-enters Earth's atmosphere'; R4: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Sources equate atmospheric entry with Entry Interface at exactly 7:53 p.m. EDT.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day milestone mission'; R3: '10-day test flight'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources consistently describe the mission as lasting 10 days.

verifications.claim: Service module separation occurred at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:33 p.m.: Crew module and service module separation'; R2: 'service module will separate around 7:33 p.m.'; R3: '7:33 p.m. EDT: Crew Module and Service Module separate'; R4: '7:33 p.m. Orion’s crew and service module have separated'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state service/crew module separation at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10.

verifications.claim: Entry Interface occurred at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m.: Entry interface'; R2: 'at 7:53 p.m.' for entry; R3: '7:53 p.m. EDT: Entry Interface occurs'; R4: '7:53 p.m. ... reached Earth’s atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly name 'Entry Interface' at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10.

verifications.claim: Reentry began at Entry Interface at approximately 400,000 ft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'As Orion descends through about 400,000 feet ... at 7:53 p.m.' (entry interface); R4: '7:53 p.m. ... reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet above'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly link Entry Interface/reaching atmosphere at ~400,000 ft.

verifications.claim: Communication blackout occurred from 7:53 p.m. to 7:59 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'six‑minute communications blackout at 7:53 p.m.'; R4: 'communications blackout expected to last about six minutes' after 7:53 p.m., '8:00 p.m. ... reestablished communications'
verifications.reasoning: Start at 7:53 p.m. and ~6-minute duration directly imply end at 7:59 p.m.; reestablish at 8:00 p.m. supports.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'planned six‑minute communications blackout'; R4: 'planned communications blackout expected to last about six minutes'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state blackout lasts six/about six minutes.

verifications.claim: Astronauts were brought aboard the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'recovery crews from the USS John P. Murtha ... transported ... back to the recovery ship'; R6: 'on board the recovery ship, the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm astronauts transported aboard USS John P. Murtha post-splashdown.
